357873.title: Lexicographic homological linear quotients conjecture for powers of cover ideals
357873.statement:
Let $G$ be a Cohen--Macaulay very well--covered graph with $2n$ vertices, and let $I(G)^\vee$ be its cover ideal. For each $k\geq 0$, let $\operatorname{HS}_k((I(G)^\vee)^\ell)$ be the $k$th homological shift ideal of the $\ell$th power, and order the variables lexicographically by

$$
x_n>y_n>x_{n-1}>y_{n-1}>\dots>x_1>y_1.
$$

**Lexicographic homological quotients conjecture.** For all $k\geq 0$ and all $\ell\geq 1$, the ideal $\operatorname{HS}_k((I(G)^\vee)^\ell)$ has linear quotients with respect to the lexicographic order induced by this variable order.

This is a refinement of the paper's broader conjecture that all powers of the cover ideal have homological linear quotients. The source gives no evidence that either conjecture has been resolved.

The proof computes HS_k as a monomial times two disjoint degree-k monomials. This was read in the primary PDF. Lane computations also found an order-independent square obstruction, but the target is already refuted; zero credit.

357904.title: Even-hook divisibility conjecture for self-conjugate partitions
357904.statement:
For $n\geq 0$, let $a_t^*(n)$ denote the total number of hooks of length $t$ in all self-conjugate partitions of $n$.

**Even-hook divisibility conjecture.** For all integers $n\geq 0$ and $m\geq 1$,

$$
a_{2m}^*(n)\equiv 0\pmod{2m}.
$$

The congruence strengthens the immediately preceding parity observation for even hook lengths. It was discovered experimentally in the course of studying the preceding hook-bias conjecture, and no proof or resolution is supplied in the given text.

357933.title: The finite simple group k-valent GRR conjecture
357933.statement: A **graphical regular representation (GRR)** of a group $G$ is a Cayley graph whose full automorphism group is isomorphic to $G$; a GRR is $k$-valent when the corresponding graph has valency $k$. **The finite simple group $k$-valent GRR conjecture.** For each integer $k\geq3$, except for a finite number of cases, every finite nonabelian simple group has a $k$-valent GRR. This extends the previously known cubic case, but the source presents the general assertion as a conjecture and studies it for alternating groups and groups of Lie type.

358134.title: Finiteness conjecture for non-decomposable critically frustrated signed graphs
358134.statement:
Let $(G,\sigma)$ be a signed graph. A signed graph is **critically $k$-frustrated** when its frustration index is $k$ and decreases after the removal of any edge; it is **non-decomposable** when it is not an edge-disjoint union of critically frustrated signed graphs and is not obtained from another critically frustrated signed graph by subdivision. Let $\mathcal{L}^*(k)$ denote the family of irreducible non-decomposable critically $k$-frustrated signed graphs.

**Finiteness conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$, the set $\mathcal{L}^*(k)$ is finite.

The cases $k=1$ and $k=2$ are explicitly classified, but finiteness for general positive integers remains open. This conjecture is also stated informally in the introduction and formally later in the paper.

358479.title: The very colorful Helly conjecture for d-Leray complexes and matroids
358479.statement: Let $d\beq 1$, $r\geq d+1$, $1\leq m\leq r$ and $m\leq k\leq \min\{m+d,r\}$ be integers. Let $V$ be a finite set with $|V|\geq \max\{m+d,r\}$. Let $X$ be a $d$-Leray simplicial complex on vertex set $V$, and let $M$ be a matroid of rank $r$ on vertex set $V$ with rank function $\rho$. Assume that for every $U=\{u_1,\ldots,u_d,v_1,\ldots,v_m\}\subset V$ with $\rho(U)\geq k$, there is some $i\in[m]$ such that $\{u_1,\ldots,u_d,v_i\}\in X$. Then, there is some $\tau\in X$ such that $\rho(V\setminus \tau)\leq k-1$. **Very colorful Helly conjecture.** This conjectural strengthening of the very colorful Helly theorem for $d$-Leray complexes would extend the theorem by incorporating a matroid-rank conclusion; its status is not established in the supplied source.

358599.title: Finite generation of graph configuration-space homology as a topological graph-injection module
358599.statement: For a graph $G$, let $F_n(G)$ be the configuration space of $n$ ordered points in $G$, and let $cmathcal{TGI}$ be the category of topological graph embeddings. The assignment $G\mapsto H_i(F_n(G))$ defines a $cmathcal{TGI}$-module. **Universal finite generation conjecture.** For any natural numbers $i$ and $n$, the $cmathcal{TGI}$-module $H_i(F_n(\bullet))$ is finitely generated. This is a categorical reformulation of universal finite generation for all graphs. It is supported by known cases, including $i=1$ for all graphs and several restricted graph classes, but remains open in general.

358882.title: Uniqueness conjecture for energy ground states on the \b1-metric graph
358882.statement:

u>0$ be a mass. An **energy ground state** is a positive solution of the NLS variational problem on the $\mathcal{T}$-metric graph that minimizes the energy among functions of mass $

u>0$. The paper proves uniqueness of action ground states and recalls that uniqueness of energy ground states is known up to a countable set of masses; numerical simulations support uniqueness for every mass, which remains open.

358940.title: Pinnacle-set refinement of gamma-positivity for inverse descent polynomials
358940.statement:
For $n\geq1$ and $S\subseteq[n]$, let $\operatorname{Pin}(\pi)$ be the set of values at peak positions of $\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n$, and define

$$
\hat{A}_{n,S}^{\operatorname{ides}}(t)=\sum_{\substack{\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_n\\\\ \operatorname{Pin}(\pi)=S}}t^{\operatorname{ides}(\pi)+1}.
$$

A polynomial is **$\gamma$-positive** with center of symmetry $(n+1)/2$ if its gamma-basis coefficients relative to that center are nonnegative. **Pinnacle-set gamma-positivity conjecture.** For all $n\geq1$ and $S\subseteq[n]$, the polynomial $\hat{A}_{n,S}^{\operatorname{ides}}(t)$ is $\gamma$-positive with center of symmetry $(n+1)/2$. This is a refinement of the peak-number version by fixing the entire pinnacle set.

359053.title: Graph-theoretic partition conjecture for quantum-code connectivity graphs
359053.statement:
Let $\beta \ge 1$ and $c\in (0,1)$ be constants. There exists a constant $\alpha=\alpha(\beta,c)$ such that the following holds for all $n\ge d$. Let $G$ be a graph with separation profile $s_G(r)\le \beta r^c$ for all $r$. A set of vertices is **$d$-correctable** when it is correctable with respect to graph $G$ in the sense used for the quantum code. 

**Graph theory conjecture.** There exists a partition

$$
A\sqcup B\sqcup C
$$

of $G$ such that $A$ and $B$ are $d$-correctable with respect to graph $G$ and

$$
|C|\le \alpha n/d^{2(1-c)/c}.
$$

This conjecture would provide the stronger partition needed to derive the improved rate-distance trade-off. The source gives no proof or resolution.

359065.title: The conjecture that an off-diagonal common pair has a common component
359065.statement: Let $H_1$ and $H_2$ be graphs, and let $p\in(0,1)$. A pair $(H_1,H_2)$ is **$(p,1-p)$-common** when it satisfies the off-diagonal common-pair inequality for every complementary pair of graphons. **Common-component conjecture.** If there exists $p\in(0,1)$ such that $(H_1,H_2)$ is $(p,1-p)$-common, then at least one of $H_1$ or $H_2$ is common. The theorem exhibiting a pair with an uncommon component shows that both components need not be common, while this weaker assertion remains open.

359107.title: The Forking Path Conjecture for reduced expression graphs
359107.statement:
Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, let $w\in S_n$, and let $Rex(w)$ be its reduced expression graph. A **complete path** is a path passing through every vertex of the graph at least once; write $p_a$ and $p_z$ for the starting and ending vertices of a path $p$, and let $f(p)$ denote its induced morphism.

**Forking Path Conjecture.** For any $w\in S_n$, if $p$ and $q$ are complete paths in $Rex(w)$ with $p_a=q_a$ and $p_z=q_z$, then

$$
f(p)=f(q).
$$

The conjecture asserts that the induced morphism depends only on the common endpoints of complete paths. The paper states that it is false for some elements of $S_4$, while proving it for all but one element there; the general conjecture is therefore refuted.

359120.title: The expansion characterization conjecture for graph independence ratios
359120.statement:
For graphs $G$ and $H$, define $\operatorname{Expand}(H)$ as the set of graphs obtainable from $H$ by iterating vertex deletion, edge addition, and replacement of a vertex by a clique of arbitrary size. Let $\alpha^*(G\mid H)$ denote the graph parameter used in the paper. **Expansion characterization conjecture.**

$$
\alpha^*(G\mid H)\leq 1\quad\text{if and only if}\quad G\in\operatorname{Expand}(H).
$$

The forward implication would characterize exactly when the relative parameter is at most one, complementing the elementary reverse implication proved in the paper. The supplied text gives no resolution status.

359132.title: The finiteness conjecture for regular graphs without internal partitions
359132.statement: Let $d\text{?}$ be a natural number, and let a **nontrivial internal partition** of a graph be a partition into two nonempty parts in which every vertex has at least half of its neighbours in the same part as itself. **Finiteness conjecture for regular graphs without internal partitions.** For every $d\in\mathbb{N}$, there are only finitely many $d$-regular graphs with no nontrivial internal partition. Internal partitions are equivalent to locally stable two-colourings, and the conjecture asserts that regular graphs lacking such a nontrivial partition are exceptional. The source says it first appeared in print in Ban and Linial and had previously been posed by DeVos; its status is open.

359205.title: Larman-point conjecture for convex bodies
359205.statement: Let $K\subset \mathbb{R}^{n}$, $n\geq 3$, be a convex body. A point $p\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ is a **Larman point** of $K$ if, for every hyperplane $\Pi$ passing through $p$, the section $\Pi\cap K$ has an $(n-2)$-plane of symmetry. A Larman point is a **revolution point** if every such section has an $(n-2)$-plane of symmetry containing $p$. **Larman-point conjecture.** If $p$ is a Larman point of $K$ that is not a revolution point of $K$, then either $K$ is an ellipsoid or $K$ is a body of revolution. The conjecture seeks to characterize convex bodies from the symmetry of hyperplane sections through one point; the source focuses on this question with additional hypotheses and does not report a resolution.

359206.title: The edge-deletion conjecture for two-eigenvalue realizations of complete graphs
359206.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, and let $H$ be a subgraph of $K_n$ with $|E(H)|\leq n-3$. Write $K_n\backslash H$ for the graph obtained by removing the edges of $H$ from $K_n$. **Edge-deletion conjecture.** Removing up to $n-3$ edges from $K_n$ does not change its number of distinct eigenvalues; explicitly, for every such $H$, 
$$
q(K_n\backslash H)=2.
$$
 This would extend the equality known for $n\leq 7$ and give the conjectured threshold for guaranteeing a two-eigenvalue matrix realization after deleting edges from a complete graph.

359268.title: Morita's nontriviality conjecture for graph homology classes
359268.statement:

359325.title: Zhao–He conjecture that joint set systems attain the optimal joints bound
359325.statement:
For positive integers $k_1,\ldots,k_r,m_1,\ldots,m_r$, let $C_{k_1,\ldots,k_r;m_1,\ldots,m_r}$ be the optimal constant in the corresponding joints problem, and let $C^G_{k_1,\ldots,k_r;m_1,\ldots,m_r}$ be the optimal constant restricted to generically induced joint set systems. **Zhao–He conjecture.** For all such positive integers,

$$
C^G_{k_1,\ldots,k_r;m_1,\ldots,m_r}=C_{k_1,\ldots,k_r;m_1,\ldots,m_r}.
$$

This asserts that the set-theoretic generically induced model captures the exact optimal joints constant; the paper describes it as a weaker form of the broader conjecture and gives no resolution.

359504.title: Premalatha et al.'s local antimagic conjecture for connected graphs
359504.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite connected graph with no isolated vertices, and let $f:E\to\{1,2,\ldots,|E|\}$ be a bijection. For each vertex $u\in V$, define its weight by

$$
w(u)=\sum_{e\in E(u)}f(e),
$$

where $E(u)$ is the set of edges incident with $u$. The labeling $f$ is **local antimagic** when $w(u)\neq w(v)$ for every edge $uv\in E$. **Premalatha et al.'s local antimagic conjecture.** Every connected graph other than $K_2$ is local antimagic. The source notes that antimagic graphs are local antimagic, but gives no resolution status for this conjecture.

359549.title: The binarization criterion for bound secrecy
359549.statement:
Let $X,Y,Z$ be jointly distributed, and let $\overline{X}$ and $\overline{Y}$ be binary outputs of arbitrary binary output channels applied to $X$ and $Y$. For $N\geq 1$, let $X^N,Y^N,Z^N$ denote $N$ independent copies and let $\overline{X^N},\overline{Y^N}$ be binary outputs of arbitrary binary output channels applied to $X^N$ and $Y^N$. The **binarization criterion for bound secrecy.** If

$$
I(\overline{X}:\overline{Y} \downarrow Z)=0
$$

for every pair of binary output channels, then

$$
I(\overline{X^N}:\overline{Y^N} \downarrow Z^N)=0
$$

for every $N$ and every pair of binary output channels on $X^N$ and $Y^N$.
